clue.text: Clumsy person breaking section in wall

indicators.note: something breaking into another thing splits it open and sits inside it

blocks.note: a section is a part of something
an ape is a clumsy, oafish person

explanation.surface: A clumsy builder knocks through a stretch of wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Exercises on record oddly involving monarch and hierarchy

indicators.note: doing something oddly means doing it in a strange way, so these letters come out jumbled
to involve something is to take it in, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
the word record, its letters rearranged
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A workout set to music somehow ends up featuring royalty and rank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the exercises sit at the top of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecking order is an informal ranking of status within a group, named after dominance among hens.

clue.text: Agent with service admitting large defeat

indicators.note: admitting something means letting it in, so one word holds another inside

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
use, as in being of service
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sales agent offering service suffers a big setback.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attacker is to drive them back, beating off the assault.

clue.text: Agreeably different panel last year

indicators.note: made different, these letters take on a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Last year's committee was nicer company than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe doing something in a pleasing, agreeable manner.

clue.text: River in wood, miles away

indicators.note: something sent away is no longer present, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: timber is wood
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A river runs through a forest, miles from anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome in central Italy.

clue.text: Discourage delay

blocks.note: first meaning: to deter or dissuade someone
second meaning: to postpone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both deterring someone from acting and postponing an event until later.

clue.text: Prepared to erupt if getting little cake?

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A volcano on standby, primed to blow if it gets a fancy dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is absurd; the definition is simply the final two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit four is a tiny fancy cake or biscuit served after a meal; French for small oven.

clue.text: Attempt to encapsulate love for city of Paris?

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone tries to capture romance in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris here is not the French capital but the Trojan prince whose elopement with Helen started the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Paris was a prince and son of King Priam, ruler of that ancient city.

clue.text: Flower father planted on raised area, I notice

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something reads it from the bottom upward

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written
to see is to notice

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a flower Dad planted on a raised bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted on' puts FR on top of the rest in this down entry; raised turns the following three pieces upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are fragrant South African plants of the iris family grown for their trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Reliable police officer with watchword back in base

indicators.note: going back means reading the word in the opposite direction
one word placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: copper is informal British slang for a police officer
a bed is a base, as in a riverbed or flowerbed
a watchword is a motto or slogan

explanation.surface: A dependable cop at headquarters keeps the station's slogan close.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships were once sheathed with copper below the waterline for protection, so the term came to mean thoroughly sound and dependable.

clue.text: No admittance after development is polluted

indicators.note: after development the original form has changed, so the letters appear in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A building site sealed off from the public because the land is toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted and tainted ground or water has been made impure by harmful substances.

clue.text: Left with desire to disrupt mad show

indicators.note: to disrupt something is to break into it, so letters are pushed inside

blocks.note: mad in the sense of angry
L is the abbreviation for left
lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A disgruntled spectator's passion wrecks a crazy performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate a point is to demonstrate or exhibit it with examples or pictures.

clue.text: Ring linked to odd elements in sale of capital

indicators.note: the odd elements are the first, third and fifth characters of the following words

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
keep the first, third and fifth characters

explanation.surface: A jeweller's ring goes on sale in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection runs across two words, so 'of' is fodder, not a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by example: the Norwegian seat of government, a classic short European city answer.

clue.text: Benefit in advancement for young person

indicators.note: one word placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: an ascent is a rise or advancement
the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Welfare payments help a teenager get ahead in life.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, someone between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Learn good tip

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to tip is to lean or tilt

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a useful piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good tip' reads as a helpful hint, but tip is the verb meaning to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean information is to gather or find it out gradually, much as gleaners gather leftover grain.

clue.text: Air in large shed

blocks.note: broad means wide or large
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Fresh air circulating in a big garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like a noun, the outbuilding, but it is the verb to discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme is to transmit it on radio or television.

clue.text: Book entirely about loud insect

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one word surrounds another

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
utterly means entirely
f is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A book devoted entirely to a noisy bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly is a winged insect with large, brightly coloured wings.

clue.text: Controller's true goal ruined by resistance

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A manager's real aim is spoilt by opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a person, body or device that controls or governs something.

clue.text: Something with which chap covers part of body?

definitions.text: Something with which chap covers part of body?

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so one word encloses another

blocks.note: a gent is a chap
the arm is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a man wears to cover himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a man puts on clothing to cover his body.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is an item of clothing, which is what anyone uses to cover the body.

clue.text: Substitute returning pass with doubtful expression

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
um is a hesitant noise of doubt

explanation.surface: A stand-in footballer sends back a pass, looking unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in temporarily for another.

clue.text: Language used by machines extensively

indicators.note: the letters are used by the following words, which contain them in sequence

blocks.note: the run of letters spans both words

explanation.surface: A programming language that machines run on widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese is the language family of China, including Mandarin and Cantonese.

clue.text: Gain vase, according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: Profit from a vase, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money or respect is to gain it through work or merit.

clue.text: Pressure to join in courses arranged for part of orchestra

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Students are pressed to sign up for classes to play in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion section is the group of drums, cymbals and similar instruments in an orchestra.

clue.text: Disagree with Conservative whip

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: An MP falls out with the Tory party whip.
explanation.walkthrough: A party whip is the official who enforces voting discipline, but here whip is the lash.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash with someone is to argue or come into conflict with them.

clue.text: At a distance from Nadal, upset?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: Rafa is the familiar first name of Rafael Nadal, the Spanish tennis champion

explanation.surface: Watching a beaten tennis star from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue needs the player's first name, not his surname: Rafael Nadal is known as Rafa.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away, from or at a great distance.

clue.text: Fellows taken in by devious effect, false modesty

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so the letters wander from their order
something taken in by another is held inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Men fooled by a trick, showing a modest manner they don't really feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False modesty' looks like the definition, but false belongs to the fodder; only modesty defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-effacement is keeping oneself in the background out of humility, a form of modesty.

clue.text: Level enclosure filled with mineral

indicators.note: something filled with another holds it inside

blocks.note: a sty is a pig enclosure
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A flat pen stuffed with rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: each floor of a building sits at one height, so a floor and a level are the same thing.

clue.text: Article in store, not right for impetuous type

indicators.note: one word placed in another is enclosed by it
not having something means it is removed

blocks.note: a hoard is a store or stockpile
R is the abbreviation for right
the definite article

explanation.surface: A shop item that's wrong for a rash shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' is a separate instruction acting on the store; the article goes inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is a rash, quick-tempered person who acts without thinking.
